biography.plain_text: Pete Whittier was an American beneficiary of the Whittier family's California oil fortune, whose roots lay in Belridge Oil. A son of Paul Whittier, he lived in Montana before making a home on Washington's Orcas Island. His local giving included donating land for the island's Orcas Village fire station in 1981.

long_biography.plain_text:
Pete Whittier raised buffalo on a small ranch on Orcas Island, taking visiting family-office staff out to see the herd in an open Jeep. One of the animals was a bull named Zeus. On one visit, his passengers arrived spattered with mud from the ride, an inconvenience that did not concern their host.

He left the detailed management of his investments to professionals. During a market downturn, he telephoned Bill Ramsey, who headed Whittier's Nevada operation, to ask whether his wealth remained secure. Reassured that it did, he ended the call without requesting a detailed review of his holdings.
